explanation: Standard form gives P(x)=1/[x(x+1)] and Q(x)=ln(x)/(x-9). At x=3 both are analytic, so it is ordinary. At x=0, x^2Q(x)=x^2ln(x)/(x-9) has no analytic extension, so it is irregular singular. At x=9, (x-9)P and (x-9)^2Q are analytic, so it is regular singular. The classification at x=-1 requires clarification: real ln(x) is undefined near -1, so no supplied classification applies to the real equation. If a local complex logarithm branch is allowed, -1 is regular singular, corresponding to option 1.

answers.correct_value: Undefined for the real equation; a regular singular point if a local complex logarithm branch is allowed.
